plan.name: Run Python checks with application dependencies
plan.summary: Build and reuse Python application images from project-root requirements.txt and every recursive local requirement or constraint input on the existing digest-pinned Python base for linux/amd64, installing only public-PyPI wheels, allowing installation network only during image construction, and stopping on installation or evidence failure without falling back to standard-library execution. Before selecting or building a dependency image, have that base’s own pip parse the application files in a network-free container with an isolated Python invocation (-I), from a clean directory with the project mounted read-only and no host environment or credentials; its complete report of requirements (names, extras, specifiers, unevaluated markers and hashes), followed files and include roles, and every other option or source form decides acceptance, with pip refusals and missing, malformed or failed reports stopping the operation. Keep every earlier strict preflight rejection and supported UTF-8, optional BOM, LF/CRLF, comment, continuation, marker, hash and local-include form, but accept only what pip reports as named PyPI requirements with hashes as their only options and includes confined to the project, rejecting links, paths, archives, URLs, editable forms and other options; generate canonical/requirements.txt and canonical/constraints.txt from that report, one requirement with its hashes per line and no comments, continuations, includes or other options, and let installation read only those literal-directory copies without rewriting application inputs. Retain recipe and cache identity over the complete recipe, base, platform, original paths and bytes and canonical filenames and bytes, isolated build-side Python and trusted absolute gate commands; install distributions with pip --target into a directory that is not a Python site directory, keep their scripts off PATH and every installed file away from gate executables and saved evidence, and run checks with the pinned base’s absolute interpreter, adding the library directory to its import path only after startup and after trusted standard-library and gate-runner paths so installed python scripts, .pth files, sitecustomize and usercustomize cannot execute or alter results without an application import; suppress Docker-client proxy configuration, including credentials and uppercase and lowercase proxy variables, for every gate container and image build without changing the user’s configuration or breaking daemon selection; retain one immutable image ID for evidence and ordinary and larger-bound runs, separate Nagini dependencies and the no-requirements standard-library path, and JSON and Markdown receipt fingerprints covering original and canonical hashes and resolved wheel names, versions, filenames and SHA-256 hashes through component attribution; cached images retain their actual resolution while fresh unpinned builds may differ, and component execution adapters, Python existing-code discovery and contract checks remain subsequent work. Preserve existing acceptance and generated-recipe coverage, adapting existing Docker-argument and output-ordering test fixtures only for proxy suppression and trusted absolute commands, retain the archive, include-parsing and parser-authority regressions, add hostile-wheel regressions for interpreter scripts and startup hooks and credential-bearing Docker proxy configuration, and make the INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 comparison check canonical files against the production pinned-pip report as well as independent pinned-pip parsing of accepted and relevant rejected fixtures; update README and SPEC.md under D-0122 for supported forms, parsing and installation isolation, proxy suppression and reproducibility, explicitly stating that imported dependencies execute as part of the application under test, with the merger running the real Docker and PyPI suite on the final pull request head and posting its passing output, recording the still-needed dependency-policy decision, and citing it with D-0013, D-0030, D-0031, D-0032, D-0054 and D-0122 as applicable in each changed SPEC bullet.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeCoversReferencedInputs
tests.says: The recipe covers the recursive requirement and constraint closure, is independent of checkout location and unrelated source, and accepts the documented wheel requirement syntax without changing input files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnaccountedInputs
tests.says: Unsupported requirement sources, escaping or symlinked paths, missing references and reference cycles fail before any dependency installation can run.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyImagesBuildReuseAndRunOffline
tests.says: A dependency image is built once and reused with its recorded wheel provenance, referenced constraints invalidate it, and Python checks use it offline; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 additionally exercises the same fixture against real Docker and PyPI.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyFailuresDoNotFallBack
tests.says: Installation failure or missing or malformed resolved artifact evidence prevents Python execution and produces an actionable error rather than a standard-library fallback.

tests.name: TestPythonGateRecordsAndReusesApplicationEnvironment
tests.says: The gate records the environment used by tests and conformance, reuses it one size larger, leaves Nagini's pinned verifier independent, and preserves projects without requirements.

tests.name: TestPythonReceiptIdentifiesResolvedDependencies
tests.says: JSON and Markdown receipts show the application base, recipe, original and canonical input hashes and resolved wheels separately from Nagini, including when reusable environment evidence is retained through component attribution.

tests.name: TestPythonFingerprintTracksResolvedDependencies
tests.says: Dependency evidence survives JSON receipts and component attribution; fingerprints bind original and canonical input hashes, platform and resolved artifacts while excluding mutable local references and execution-only image IDs.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectHiddenPipOptions
tests.says: Every non-CR/LF separator recognized by Python splitlines is rejected in root and referenced inputs before Docker can run, including options hidden after a comment.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesPinImageAcrossTagReplacement
tests.says: Even when a concurrent build replaces the recipe tag between selection, evidence reads, tests and larger-bound checks, all reads and runs use one immutable image ID and the receipt describes that image.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeIsolatesInputModules
tests.says: Build-side Python uses isolated mode and a clean working directory; with INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 the generated recipe actually builds and runs offline despite referenced venv.py and pip.py files that fail if executed.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeCopiesLiteralFilenames
tests.says: Distinct [a].txt and a.txt inputs are read literally and hashed separately, flattened with their correct requirement or constraint roles, and excluded from the Docker context; the real generated recipe installs the intended package version.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesKeepGateCommandsTrusted
tests.says: Dependency-installed cat, sh and timeout cannot replace the gate evidence reader or ordinary and larger-bound checks; the real-Docker layer executes the generated recipe, installs a hostile fixture wheel offline, and verifies unchanged receipt evidence and successful and failing application checks.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesAcceptUTF8Inputs
tests.says: Root and referenced inputs accept UTF-8 with or without its leading BOM and LF or CRLF endings, retain original byte hashes and produce canonical installation files with their own hashes; the real generated recipes install the package and run offline.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectInvalidUTF8
tests.says: Invalid UTF-8 anywhere in root or referenced requirements and constraints, including comments and after a BOM, is rejected before any Docker invocation without rewriting inputs.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectBareCR
tests.says: Every CR not immediately followed by LF is rejected in root and referenced requirements and constraints before Docker, including comments, continuations and trailing bytes.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectEncodingDeclarations
tests.says: Encoding declarations in comments are rejected anywhere in every effective dependency file, even when declaring UTF-8, appearing beyond the first two lines or accompanying a BOM, before any Docker invocation.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectEncodingDeclarationExploit
tests.says: The review's raw CR and unicode_escape declaration payload, hiding either --no-binary or --index-url, is rejected before Docker in root, referenced requirement and constraint files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeResolvesTraversedDirectories
tests.says: Requirement and constraint references resolve safely through in-project directories, including empty directories canceled by .., without copying original inputs or their directory layout into the image; original hashes, canonical output, reuse and real offline execution remain correct.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnsafeTraversal
tests.says: Every directory traversed by a requirement or constraint reference must stay inside the project and avoid symlinks, even when '..' cancels that directory and the final target is an existing in-project file; unsafe paths fail before Docker.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectBackslashExploit
tests.says: The review's two-backslash marker payload hiding --no-binary or --index-url is rejected in root, recursively referenced requirements and constraints before Docker, with application inputs unchanged.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnsupportedBackslashes
tests.says: Runs of backslashes, dangling continuations and backslashes anywhere except a single trailing continuation are rejected in every effective input before any Docker invocation.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnsupportedGrammar
tests.says: Malformed requirements, extras, versions, markers, includes and hashes, unparsed suffixes and forbidden options including those hidden in quoted markers or single continuations fail before Docker instead of reaching pip.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesCanonicalizeAcceptedRequirements
tests.says: Canonical files preserve accepted names, extras, versions, compound markers and hashes while flattening recursive includes, keeping requirement and constraint roles distinct even for shared inputs, and removing comments and continuations without changing original files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesCanonicalCacheTracksBothRepresentations
tests.says: Original input changes invalidate reuse even when canonical bytes stay identical, while effective changes update canonical hashes and resolution; restored or unchanged inputs reuse the same recorded environment.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeReadsOnlyCanonicalFiles
tests.says: Only canonical requirements and constraints reach the generated recipe; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 executes production builds and the captured unmodified recipe, verifies offline imports and actual wheel evidence, and proves canonical hashes and constraints control installation through failure cases.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesJoinContinuationsWithoutInsertedCharacters
tests.says: Single continuations preserve pip's exact logical text without adding or removing spaces, including the review's split posix marker and split names, versions and hashes, in root and referenced requirements and constraints with LF or CRLF and optional BOM; canonical evidence, reuse and original bytes remain correct.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesAcceptCodingPackageNames
tests.says: geocoding==1.0 and coding text in names or markers are accepted in every effective-file role and supported encoding, while encoding declarations in comments remain rejected anywhere before Docker runs.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesMatchPinnedPipParser
tests.says: With INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 every accepted fixture runs production’s pinned-pip invocation offline; its requirement identities, unevaluated markers, hashes, followed files, literal includes and constraint roles agree with canonical files and an independent pinned-pip oracle, while the shared rejected option-whitespace corpus and semantic negative controls distinguish input refusal from infrastructure failure.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectNonSpaceOptionWhitespace
tests.says: Tabs and every other non-line-breaking whitespace pip does not split, including Unicode spaces and U+001F, cannot separate requirements from --hash; root and referenced requirements and constraints fail both dependency APIs before Docker and leave originals unchanged, including mixed-space and continuation regressions.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesAcceptASCIIOptionSpaces
tests.says: Single and repeated ASCII spaces preserve hashes, markers and continuation semantics across root and referenced requirements and constraints in UTF-8 with optional BOM and LF or CRLF, retaining leading-tab indentation, canonical evidence, cache reuse and original bytes; the pinned-pip comparison checks these accepted fixtures when enabled.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectPinnedPipInterpretationGaps
tests.says: Bare wheel and source archives, empty long-option include values and no-break-space short includes are refused in root requirements and nested requirements or constraints without modifying inputs, installing dependencies or running a standard-library fallback.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesParseWithPinnedPipBeforeBuild
tests.says: Accepted recipe and image requests invoke the pinned base’s own pip offline with absolute isolated Python, a clean working directory, a read-only project and no host credentials before building; the real suite also executes that production helper on forbidden input forms to require faithful option, link, archive and editable reports or explicit pip input refusals, while projects without requirements retain their existing path.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesCanonicalFilesComeFromPipReport
tests.says: The parser’s reported requirement names, extras, specifiers, unevaluated markers and hashes determine canonical files, their evidence and cache identity while original bytes and hashes remain unchanged.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectDisallowedPipReports
tests.says: The validator rejects pip-reported links, paths, archives, URLs, editables, non-hash options, parse errors and incomplete or unsafe file/include reports before installation or execution even when a preliminary Go parse accepts the source.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesParserFailuresDoNotBuildOrFallBack
tests.says: Parser process failures and empty, malformed, incomplete or truncated reports stop both dependency APIs and Python checks with diagnostics before building or using cached evidence, on fresh and cached paths.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesTreatInstalledDistributionsAsLibraries
tests.says: Installed python scripts, .pth files, sitecustomize, usercustomize and replacement gate modules cannot run before an application import, replace trusted commands, alter receipt evidence or hide passing or failing ordinary and larger-bound checks; the real suite executes the generated recipe and installs independently hostile wheels with working takeover controls while preserving explicit application imports.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesSuppressDockerClientProxies
tests.says: Docker client proxy settings containing credentials cannot reach the pinned-pip parser, dependency build, evidence reads or ordinary and larger-bound checks; the real suite proves client-config injection with a negative control, probes actual run and build environments, executes the unchanged generated recipe, verifies reuse and receipt evidence, and leaves the original client configuration and application files unchanged.
